_rules: Money never moves: the price rides the FIRST piece and every other piece is 0. Lines are matched to target pieces and UPDATED in place so a row id - and any purchase allocation hanging off it - survives. A document can hold MORE THAN ONE sofa build, so desc2Match is required; where a document holds TWO lines with the SAME text those are two identical sofas and both take the build. Where a document holds two sofas that NO needle can tell apart - because one build's text is a strict SUFFIX of the other's - the second build carries a `desc2Exclude` as well: the rows carrying that text, byte-exactly, are not this build. An exclusion that matches no row on the document is a REFUSAL, never a quiet widening back onto both sofas.

The account book states the same build text TWICE on SO-012025, once with a LEADING SPACE (DtlKey 829179) and once without (829180), and the ERP explodes each into four compartment rows that inherit their lead's text verbatim. The second sofa's text is therefore a strict SUFFIX of the first's, so every substring that finds the second also finds the first - proved exhaustively in scripts/lib/sofa-desc2-match.test.mjs, not assumed. So this build is addressed by what it is NOT: desc2Exclude takes out the rows carrying the leading space, byte-exactly, leaving DtlKey 829180's four rows. An exclusion that matches nothing REFUSES rather than widening back onto both sofas. | THE MONEY DOES NOT MOVE. The three surplus rows are the ones nothing points at - HC-PO-009024's 1NA, CNR and 1A(RHF) lines are all undedicated and unreceived - and the applier refuses the build outright if that stops being true. | HC-PO-009024 is named with the sales order so the pair is corrected together and the factory document does not keep building a four-piece sofa the customer document no longer says (docs/bugs/0719).
